close_reason: Documented Unknown dispatch contract precondition on the variant rustdoc; added pin test covering the three recognised dispatch paths. Behaviour is intentional (Unknown is for shapes the dispatcher does not recognise) and now documented + regression-pinned. Commit 02a532d.
description:
A Rust-side caller constructing AnniversaryDate::Unknown wrapping a
serde_json::Value that happens to be an object with a known @type (or
no @type at all) will not survive a serialize-then-deserialize
round-trip as Unknown — it will land on the matching typed variant.

Inverse of sgrr.9 (which fixed non-object Values landing in Unknown
not round-tripping). sgrr.9 closed the non-object asymmetry; this
finding documents the unaddressed object-with-known-@type asymmetry.

Trace, reading lib.rs:1034-1076:

1. let original = AnniversaryDate::Unknown(
       json!({\"@type\": \"PartialDate\", \"year\": 2000}));
2. Serialize impl at lib.rs:1039 emits the JSON Value verbatim:
       {\"@type\": \"PartialDate\", \"year\": 2000}
3. Deserialize impl at lib.rs:1054 sees is_object() = true.
4. v.get(\"@type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) returns Some(\"PartialDate\").
5. Match arm at lib.rs:1066 routes to PartialDate variant.
6. Result: AnniversaryDate::PartialDate(PartialDate {
       at_type: Some(\"PartialDate\"), year: Some(2000), ... })

Variant identity lost. Similarly for Some(\"Timestamp\")-tagged
Values, and for {} (empty object, no @type, routes to default
PartialDate with all-None fields).

Why the caller cares:

- The doc on AnniversaryDate::Unknown (lib.rs:1018-1031) claims
  preservation for round-trip fidelity: \"Carries the raw
  serde_json::Value so a future-spec @type variant ... round-trips
  losslessly\". The lossless guarantee silently holds only when the
  inner Value's @type is one the deserialize impl does NOT recognise.
- A composing caller (e.g. building a partial Card from multiple
  upstream sources) who wraps an arbitrary date-shaped Value in
  Unknown has no compile-time or runtime signal that the wrapping
  will be undone on the next round-trip.
- The doc comment does not state the precondition \"Value must have
  @type set to a string NOT in {None, \\\"PartialDate\\\", \\\"Timestamp\\\"}
  or be a non-object\". The contract for callers wrapping known
  shapes is undocumented.

Two ways to address (callers cannot fix this in their code; this is
a contract decision):

(a) Document the precondition explicitly on AnniversaryDate::Unknown
    rustdoc: \"Unknown is intended for unknown @type values only.
    Construct via Unknown(v) where v is either non-object or has
    @type set to a value not in {\\\"PartialDate\\\", \\\"Timestamp\\\"}.
    Wrapping a recognised shape will lose variant identity across
    serialize-then-deserialize.\"
(b) Reject construction at the API boundary: make the variant
    pub(crate) and expose a fallible AnniversaryDate::unknown(v) ->
    Result<Self, _> that validates the precondition. (Breaking,
    requires major-version bump.)

Probe to confirm under /do-beads (cannot run in read-only review):

    #[test]
    fn unknown_object_with_known_at_type_loses_variant_identity() {
        let original = AnniversaryDate::Unknown(
            serde_json::json!({\"@type\": \"PartialDate\", \"year\": 2000}));
        let wire = serde_json::to_value(&original).unwrap();
        let back: AnniversaryDate =
            serde_json::from_value(wire).unwrap();
        // Documents the asymmetry, not asserts the desired shape:
        assert!(!matches!(back, AnniversaryDate::Unknown(_)),
            \"contract gap: variant identity lost across round-trip\");
    }

Recommendation: option (a). The breaking change in (b) is large for
a 0.1.x kit crate and the documented precondition is sufficient if
callers are warned. Filed at P2 because no spec-conformant wire
input triggers this (RFC 9553 emitters do not produce
Unknown-tagged dates with @type set to a known kind), but a Rust-
side composing caller can hit it without warning.
title: AnniversaryDate::Unknown(object-with-known-@type) round-trips to typed variant, not Unknown
